# Company research comes before choosing the motion

The user can ask for a new iMessage launch video for any company. This is an instruction for the agent to research, direct and implement the work using its actual tools. The library is not an autonomous research model or a button that invents company facts.

1. Resolve the actual company/product and official domain from the prompt. Search supplied/connected context, the official site and primary docs. If a name such as “Open Commerce on Katy” is ambiguous, investigate before assuming what it means; ask one focused clarification only if credible alternatives remain.
2. Read product, audience, core promise, actual user action and proof of success. Prefer first-party documentation and real UI to unsourced summaries. Record source URL/title, retrieval date, exact supporting passage, and whether each fact is observed, inferred or unresolved.
3. Inventory brand and product visuals: logo, fonts/licenses, colors, screenshots, UI states, messages, cards and genuine content. Capture relevant screens when available and permitted. Keep source/bounds/hashes for extracted assets. Do not fabricate a payment, booking, integration, price or result the product does not support.
4. Produce a compact company research profile using company-profile.schema.json. Explain the strongest video story supported by the evidence and list remaining asset gaps. Keep the evidence ledger alongside the project so copy claims can be checked.
5. Choose a causal story: need → request → useful response → embedded action → visible result, or a different arc justified by the promise. Use a wall when breadth is the point; use an embedded app when completing work inside the conversation is the point. Decorative motion must support the story.
6. Inspect the selected visual atlas and full accepted example project. The registry pairs source, assets, real method implementations, reference movie, finished results, frame metrics and provenance. Retrieve the smallest complete project needed. Download full history only for diagnosis or deeper extraction; do not load gigabytes of code into the model context at once.
7. Write a shot plan with exact copy, source-backed claims, named components, stable actor identity, attention target, local/camera transforms, clipping, action phases, reading holds and UI sound anchors. Explain the chosen motion and an alternative's tradeoff. The nine starters and fourteen measured studies are real entries; do not invent “seventy tools.”
8. Adapt editable components and inspect actual produced stills. Raster-rich card interiors or source-specific glyph outlines cannot be edited by changing a text string; supply new measured geometry/artwork for the new company. The complete source demonstrates the technique without granting editability it does not have.
9. Render through the actual available method adapters. Compare native frames and geometry, inspect high-error transitions, then review UI sound alone before adding optional music. Log the cause and changed variable before retrying a failure.
10. Deliver research/evidence, shot plan, complete scene/assets/code, method/runtime versions, final video, sound stems, comparisons and known limits. Add the new example to the private library with hashes and its rendered visual reference. Do not change sharing or make private source/font inputs public without explicit user authorization.

For exact recreation of a supplied film, its native source geometry/timing remains the authority. A new-company adaptation is newly directed work, not an exact recreation of a source brand's film. Figma is marked unavailable/unvalidated until an actual motion/export capability succeeds; the included prototype is not a finished sixth renderer.
